bank_a_signs.prompt: What is the mandatory driver response when approaching an octagonal red MUTCD R1-1 STOP sign?

options.text: Come to a complete stop before the stop line, crosswalk, or entering intersection
Slow down to five miles per hour and roll through if cross traffic is not visible
Stop only if approaching vehicles from the right arrive at the intersection first
Tap your vehicle horn to alert surrounding pedestrians before driving through

bank_a_signs.rationale: Under TTC §544.004 and MUTCD R1-1, an operator facing a stop sign must come to a complete stop at the stop line, crosswalk, or intersection boundary.

bank_a_signs.prompt: What does an inverted triangular red-and-white MUTCD R1-2 YIELD sign legally require of a driver?

options.text: Slow down and yield right-of-way to all vehicles and pedestrians on roadway
Come to a mandatory complete stop regardless of whether any other traffic is present
Accelerate quickly to enter before approaching main road vehicles reach junction
Yield right-of-way exclusively to commercial freight vehicles and city buses

bank_a_signs.rationale: Under TTC §545.151, an operator facing a yield sign must slow to a reasonable speed and yield right-of-way to any vehicle or pedestrian in or approaching the intersection.

bank_a_signs.prompt: What does a yellow diamond sign depicting a skidding vehicle (MUTCD W8-5) indicate to motorists?

options.text: Roadway surface ahead is slippery when wet; reduce speed and steer smoothly
A winding mountain road begins ahead with consecutive sharp hairpin turns
Pavement ends ahead and transitions into an unpaved loose gravel surface
High-speed drifting and performance driving maneuvers are authorized ahead

bank_a_signs.rationale: MUTCD W8-5 warns that road surface friction drops significantly when wet. Drivers should decelerate and avoid harsh braking or sudden steering.

bank_a_signs.prompt: What specific roadway environment is designated exclusively by an upright pentagonal traffic sign?

options.text: A public school zone, school crosswalk corridor, or child pedestrian crossing
An active railway grade crossing with multiple industrial train tracks
A mandatory state commercial vehicle weight and safety inspection station
A county emergency fire department station with exiting rescue vehicles

bank_a_signs.rationale: An upright pentagon (house-shaped) sign is reserved exclusively for school zones and school crossings to warn motorists of children and pedestrian traffic.

bank_a_signs.prompt: What is the legal mandate when encountering a square white sign with a red circle and white bar?

options.text: Do Not Enter; entry is prohibited because traffic is moving toward your vehicle
Authorized passenger vehicles may enter during daytime non-peak hours
Stop completely, sound horn twice, and proceed if roadway appears clear
Commercial transport trucks must detour into the adjacent right shoulder

bank_a_signs.rationale: MUTCD R5-1 'Do Not Enter' marks one-way roads or freeway ramps where vehicles traveling in the wrong direction would confront oncoming traffic.

bank_a_signs.prompt: What does a rectangular white regulatory sign displaying 'SPEED LIMIT 70' represent in Texas?

options.text: Maximum legal speed under ideal conditions; speed must be reduced if hazards exist
The minimum mandatory cruising speed that all passenger vehicles must maintain
A suggested advisory travel speed recommended exclusively during daylight
A speed limit that applies only to commercial interstate freight haulers

bank_a_signs.rationale: Under TTC §545.352 and §545.351, a speed limit sign establishes maximum legal speed under ideal conditions. Drivers must reduce speed below the limit when adverse conditions exist.

bank_a_signs.prompt: What does a yellow diamond sign with two converging arrows (MUTCD W4-1) indicate to drivers?

options.text: Entering traffic is merging from the right; adjust speed and position to blend flow
The travel lane divides ahead into two separate one-way divided highways
Vehicles on the main highway must come to a complete stop to let traffic merge
All vehicles must make an immediate sharp right turn at the next cross street

bank_a_signs.rationale: MUTCD W4-1 warns drivers that another lane is joining their roadway from the right. Both through traffic and merging drivers should adjust speed and spacing.

bank_a_signs.prompt: What does a white X-shaped 'RAILROAD CROSSING' crossbuck sign (MUTCD R15-1) require of drivers?

options.text: Yield right-of-way to approaching trains and stop 15 to 50 feet away if train nears
Accelerate across the tracks quickly before warning bells begin to sound
Stop on the tracks and look both ways before proceeding across the crossing
Yield to trains only when electronic red lights are actively flashing overhead

bank_a_signs.rationale: The crossbuck sign has the legal status of a YIELD sign. Under TTC §545.251, drivers must yield to trains and stop within 15 to 50 feet if a train is approaching.

bank_a_signs.prompt: What does an overhead flashing circular RED traffic light require of an approaching driver?

options.text: Complete stop at the stop line, yield to cross traffic, then proceed safely
Slow down moderately and proceed through cross street without stopping
Wait until the light cycles to solid green before advancing through junction
Treat the signal as a flashing yellow caution beacon during daytime hours

bank_a_signs.rationale: Under TTC §544.008, a flashing red signal functions identically to a stop sign: complete stop required, yield right-of-way, proceed only when clear.

bank_a_signs.prompt: What does an overhead flashing circular YELLOW traffic light indicate to motorists?

options.text: Proceed through the intersection cautiously with caution and reduced speed
Come to a complete stop and wait for a full green signal before moving
Accelerate rapidly to clear the intersection prior to signal phase shift
Switch lanes immediately away from the signal light to avoid congestion

bank_a_signs.rationale: Under TTC §544.008(b), an operator facing a flashing yellow signal may proceed through the intersection or past the signal only with caution.

bank_a_signs.prompt: What does an orange diamond-shaped highway sign signify to Texas motorists under work zone rules?

options.text: Temporary highway construction, maintenance work, or altered roadway ahead
Permanent state park or recreational campground attraction located nearby
Commercial industrial manufacturing corridor with high acoustic noise levels
Interstate route guidance directing drivers toward international toll borders

bank_a_signs.rationale: Orange signs are designated exclusively for temporary traffic control in construction and maintenance work zones, warning of workers, machinery, detours, and lane closures.

bank_a_signs.prompt: What does a solid double yellow centerline painted down the middle of a two-lane road indicate?

options.text: Passing is strictly prohibited in both directions of travel along that section
Passing is permitted for passenger cars but prohibited for commercial trucks
Traffic travels in the same direction on both sides of the double yellow line
Vehicles may cross the line at high speed to pass slow agricultural tractors

bank_a_signs.rationale: A solid double yellow centerline separates opposing traffic and indicates that passing is prohibited in both directions (except when making a safe left turn into a driveway).

bank_a_signs.prompt: What does a solid white line between lanes traveling in the same direction signify to motorists?

options.text: Lane changes are discouraged or hazardous; drivers should remain in their lane
Lane changes are completely prohibited under all circumstances in Texas
The adjacent travel lane is reserved exclusively for public transit vehicles
The travel lane will terminate abruptly within seventy-five feet ahead

bank_a_signs.rationale: A solid white line indicates that lane changes are discouraged due to elevated collision risk. A double solid white line indicates lane changes are strictly prohibited.

bank_a_signs.prompt: What does a steady red 'X' displayed over a highway lane control signal signify?

options.text: Lane is closed to travel; motorists must merge into an open green-arrow lane
Lane is reserved exclusively for high-occupancy transit vehicles with 4 people
Lane is designated for commercial freight trucks traveling above sixty mph
Lane may be used temporarily for rapid overtaking maneuvers during rush hour

bank_a_signs.rationale: A steady red 'X' overhead indicates the lane is closed to approaching traffic; driving in that lane is illegal and creates severe head-on collision danger.

bank_a_signs.prompt: If a vehicle stalls on train tracks, what emergency data on the blue ENS sign must you report to 911?

options.text: The railroad emergency dispatch 1-800 phone number and unique USDOT crossing ID
The municipal railroad tax rate and annual freight tonnage financial numbers
The historical year the train crossing was originally paved with asphalt
The manufacturer serial number of the overhead train crossing gate arms

bank_a_signs.rationale: The blue Emergency Notification System (ENS) sign contains the 24/7 railroad dispatch phone number and the unique 6-digit crossing ID plus letter to halt all oncoming train traffic.

bank_a_signs.prompt: What does a square red-and-white MUTCD R5-1 DO NOT ENTER sign indicate to motorists?

options.text: Traffic is prohibited from entering this roadway or ramp in the driver's current direction
Vehicles may enter only if gross vehicle weight is below three tons
Entry is permitted during daylight hours but restricted between sunset and sunrise
Drivers must come to a temporary stop before accelerating onto the incoming freeway lane

bank_a_signs.rationale: Under TX MUTCD R5-1, DO NOT ENTER prohibits all traffic from entering a prohibited roadway or ramp where opposing traffic travels.

bank_a_signs.prompt: What does a black-and-white rectangular sign displaying an arrow and 'ONE WAY' (MUTCD R6-1) mean?

options.text: Vehicular traffic must proceed exclusively in the direction indicated by the arrow
Traffic may travel both directions but passing is prohibited in all lanes
Only one vehicle may enter the roadway at a time under meter control
The roadway ends ahead and vehicles must execute a mandatory U-turn

bank_a_signs.rationale: Under TTC §545.059, an operator on a one-way roadway must drive only in the direction designated by signs.

bank_a_signs.prompt: What does a yellow diamond sign depicting a median barrier with traffic arrows on both sides (MUTCD W6-1) indicate?

options.text: The highway ahead becomes a divided roadway with opposing traffic separated by a physical median
The highway ends ahead and transitions into an unpaved rural gravel road
Drivers must immediately exit to the right-hand frontage road
Toll collection booths are positioned across all highway lanes ahead

bank_a_signs.rationale: MUTCD W6-1 alerts motorists that the single roadway is dividing into two separated one-way roadways with opposing traffic.

bank_a_signs.prompt: What does a yellow diamond sign depicting traffic arrows merging together around a median barrier (MUTCD W6-2) mean?

options.text: The divided highway ends ahead; two-way traffic resumes on an undivided single roadway
A multi-lane interstate highway begins ahead with high-speed express lanes
All motorists must immediately merge into the far right lane
A commercial truck weighing station is situated 500 feet ahead

bank_a_signs.rationale: MUTCD W6-2 warns motorists that the physical separation between opposing traffic lanes is ending and two-way undivided roadway resumes.

bank_a_signs.prompt: What does a yellow diamond sign depicting a large straight arrow with a smaller curved arrow joining it (MUTCD W4-1) indicate?

options.text: Traffic from another roadway is merging into your flow; adjust speed and positioning smoothly
Your lane is ending immediately and you must make a complete stop before merging
Main highway traffic must yield unconditionally to vehicles on incoming ramps
A sharp 90-degree right turn begins 100 feet ahead

bank_a_signs.rationale: MUTCD W4-1 alerts drivers on through highways that incoming traffic from an on-ramp or side lane is merging into the traffic flow.

bank_a_signs.prompt: What does a yellow diamond sign showing the right boundary line tapering inward (MUTCD W4-2 LANE ENDS) mean?

options.text: The right lane is terminating ahead; drivers in that lane must safely merge left
The road narrows into a single lane in both directions of travel
Drivers must pull off onto the right shoulder and wait for pilot car escorts
High-occupancy vehicle lanes are open to all traffic regardless of passengers

bank_a_signs.rationale: MUTCD W4-2 indicates that the right lane is ending and drivers must merge into the adjacent open lane.

bank_a_signs.prompt: What does a fluorescent yellow-green pentagon sign depicting two walking figures (MUTCD S1-1) signify?

options.text: A school zone or school pedestrian crosswalk is ahead; reduce speed and watch for children
A public jogging and bicycling recreational trail crosses the highway ahead
Pedestrians are prohibited from crossing this roadway under municipal code
Drivers may maintain posted speed limits regardless of children on curbs

bank_a_signs.rationale: Under TX MUTCD S1-1, a fluorescent yellow-green pentagon is reserved exclusively for school zones and school advance crossings.

bank_a_signs.prompt: What does a red rectangular sign with white lettering displaying 'WRONG WAY' (MUTCD R5-1a) indicate?

options.text: You are traveling against the legal flow of traffic; stop immediately and turn around safely
You are exceeding the advisory highway speed limit by more than 15 miles per hour
The roadway ahead is currently closed for routine scheduled bridge maintenance
GPS navigation devices have calculated an inaccurate roadway destination

bank_a_signs.rationale: WRONG WAY signs supplement DO NOT ENTER signs. If seen, the driver is heading directly into oncoming traffic.

bank_a_signs.prompt: What does a yellow diamond sign depicting red, yellow, and green traffic lights (MUTCD W3-3) mean?

options.text: A traffic control signal is ahead; be prepared to stop if the light is red or changing
A multi-way stop-sign-controlled intersection begins 200 feet ahead
An electronic red light automated enforcement camera is active ahead
The traffic light ahead operates exclusively as a flashing yellow warning beacon

bank_a_signs.rationale: MUTCD W3-3 warns of an upcoming signalized intersection that may have obstructed sight distance.

bank_a_signs.prompt: What does a square white sign showing a curved U-turn arrow enclosed in a red circle with a slash (MUTCD R3-4) mean?

options.text: U-turns are prohibited at this location under all traffic conditions
U-turns are permitted exclusively for commercial delivery vans and buses
Drivers may execute a U-turn only when a green turn arrow is illuminated
A circular roundabout or traffic circle begins 500 feet ahead

bank_a_signs.rationale: Under TX MUTCD R3-4, a red circle and diagonal slash across a U-shaped arrow strictly prohibits reversing direction.

bank_a_signs.prompt: What does a yellow diamond sign showing three circular counter-clockwise arrows (MUTCD W2-6) indicate?

options.text: A circular intersection (roundabout) is ahead; yield to circulating traffic before entering
A mandatory high-speed turnaround loop begins 200 feet ahead
Vehicles must maintain a minimum speed of 45 mph while circulating
Traffic inside the circle must yield to incoming vehicles entering from side roads

bank_a_signs.rationale: MUTCD W2-6 warns of an upcoming roundabout where entering vehicles must yield right-of-way to circulating traffic.

bank_a_signs.prompt: What does a yellow diamond sign depicting a truck driving down a steep incline (MUTCD W7-1) mean?

options.text: A steep downgrade is ahead; check brakes and shift into a lower gear to control speed
Trucks and commercial vehicles are strictly prohibited from using this highway
A runaway truck escape ramp is positioned directly in the center highway lane
Road construction crews are operating heavy earthmoving machinery ahead

bank_a_signs.rationale: MUTCD W7-1 warns of a steep downhill grade where extended braking can cause brake overheating and failure.

bank_a_signs.prompt: What does a yellow diamond sign showing a sharp 90-degree right arrow (MUTCD W1-1R) indicate?

options.text: A sharp curve to the right ahead; reduce speed before entering the turn
An immediate right-hand driveway leading into an emergency service station
All motorists must execute a compulsory right turn at the next street
A dual-lane right exit ramp with an advisory speed of 55 miles per hour

bank_a_signs.rationale: MUTCD W1-1 warns of a sharp horizontal curve requiring drivers to decelerate significantly before entering.

bank_a_signs.prompt: What does a white rectangular regulatory sign showing an obstruction with an arrow curving to the right (MUTCD R4-7 KEEP RIGHT) mandate?

options.text: Drivers must pass to the right of the traffic island, median, or divider obstruction
Drivers may pass to either the left or right side of the physical divider
A right-hand passing lane is reserved exclusively for slow-moving farm vehicles
The roadway is closed to through traffic and motorists must exit right

bank_a_signs.rationale: MUTCD R4-7 directs traffic to stay to the right of physical roadway obstructions such as medians and bridge pillars.

bank_a_signs.prompt: What does a yellow diamond sign with a black plus symbol '+' (MUTCD W2-1 CROSSROAD) signify?

options.text: A four-way intersecting road crosses the highway ahead; watch for cross-traffic
A regional hospital or emergency medical treatment center is adjacent to the roadway
An authorized first aid rescue helicopter landing zone is ahead
Four lanes of traffic are converging into a single shared center turning lane

bank_a_signs.rationale: MUTCD W2-1 alerts drivers that another roadway crosses the highway ahead and vehicles may be entering or crossing.

bank_a_signs.prompt: What does a yellow diamond sign displaying '12'-6"' between top and bottom arrows (MUTCD W12-2) mean?

options.text: Low overhead clearance ahead; vehicles taller than the posted height cannot clear the structure
The highway width between lane lines is restricted to twelve feet six inches
The distance between upcoming highway exits is twelve and one-half miles
Vehicles must maintain a minimum twelve-foot following distance from the curb

bank_a_signs.rationale: MUTCD W12-2 alerts operators of tall vehicles that an overhead bridge, underpass, or structure has restricted vertical clearance.

bank_a_signs.prompt: What does a yellow diamond sign with two vertical arrows pointing in opposite directions (MUTCD W6-3) mean?

options.text: Two-way traffic ahead; opposing traffic will be traveling in the adjacent oncoming lane
Drivers may select either lane traveling in the same direction
Passing is permitted in both directions without restriction
The highway transitions into a two-lane toll plaza with cash and electronic booths

bank_a_signs.rationale: MUTCD W6-3 warns motorists leaving a one-way street or divided highway that they are entering a roadway with two-way traffic.

bank_a_signs.prompt: What does a yellow pennant-shaped sign on the left side of the road reading 'NO PASSING ZONE' (MUTCD W14-3) indicate?

options.text: Marks the beginning of a no-passing zone; do not attempt to pass other vehicles from this point
Passing is restricted only to commercial trucks carrying dangerous cargo
Advises motorists that slow-moving tractors are operating on the roadway shoulder
Marks the conclusion of a construction speed restriction zone

bank_a_signs.rationale: The yellow pennant is uniquely positioned on the left side of the road at the start of a zone where passing is prohibited.

bank_a_signs.prompt: What does a yellow diamond sign showing a leaping deer silhouette (MUTCD W11-3) alert motorists to?

options.text: Wildlife and deer frequently cross the roadway in this area; be alert especially at dawn and dusk
A state public hunting reserve where licensed hunters may cross the highway
A commercial animal petting zoo and wildlife safari tourist facility is ahead
Drivers are authorized to honk continuously to clear roadside foliage

bank_a_signs.rationale: MUTCD W11-3 alerts drivers to areas where animal crossings are frequent and unexpected collisions occur.

bank_a_signs.prompt: What does a white rectangular regulatory sign reading 'SLOWER TRAFFIC KEEP RIGHT' (MUTCD R4-3) require?

options.text: Vehicles traveling slower than normal traffic flow must stay in the right-hand lane to allow passing
All motorists must decelerate to 25 miles per hour regardless of posted speed limits
The right lane is reserved exclusively for emergency responder and law enforcement vehicles
Passing on the right is mandatory when overtaking another passenger car

bank_a_signs.rationale: Under TTC §545.051 and MUTCD R4-3, an operator moving slower than the normal flow of other traffic must drive in the right-hand lane.

bank_b_laws.domain: TRAFFIC LAWS & RULES OF THE ROAD
bank_b_laws.prompt: Under Texas Transportation Code §542.404, when are traffic fines doubled in highway work zones?

options.text: Whenever construction workers are present in the work zone and signs are posted
Exclusively when construction work is actively underway during nighttime hours
Only if a physical motor vehicle crash results in property damage or injury
Fines double only for commercial freight vehicles exceeding gross weight limits

bank_b_laws.rationale: Under TTC §542.404 and TDLR work zone rules, traffic fines double for moving violations committed in maintenance or construction zones when workers are present.

bank_b_laws.domain: TRAFFIC LAWS & RULES OF THE ROAD
bank_b_laws.prompt: What is the criminal penalty for disobeying warning signs or driving around barricades in a Texas work zone?

options.text: Class B misdemeanor punishable by fines up to $1,000 and up to 180 days in jail
Standard civil parking ticket with a ten-dollar municipal court administrative fee
Mandatory forfeiture of all personal motor vehicles to state highway funds
A verbal administrative warning issued by county environmental health units

bank_b_laws.rationale: Under TTC §472.022, driving around or removing a work zone or flood barricade is a Class B misdemeanor (fines up to $1,000 and/or jail up to 180 days, escalating if bodily injury occurs).

bank_b_laws.domain: TRAFFIC LAWS & RULES OF THE ROAD
bank_b_laws.prompt: What is a driver's legal obligation when directed by an authorized human flagger in a work zone?

options.text: Comply with flagger directions promptly; flagger instructions legally supersede signals
Flagger instructions are voluntary advice that drivers may disregard at will
Yield to flaggers only if electronic intersection traffic signals are dark
Proceed at full posted highway speed unless an armed police officer is present

bank_b_laws.rationale: TTC §542.501 makes it a traffic violation to disobey an authorized flagger. Flagger manual directions supersede standard traffic control devices to protect road workers.

bank_b_laws.domain: TRAFFIC LAWS & RULES OF THE ROAD
bank_b_laws.category: TEXAS MOVE OVER / SLOW DOWN ACT
bank_b_laws.prompt: What speed reduction is required when passing a stopped emergency or TxDOT work vehicle with flashing lights?

options.text: Slow to 20 mph below posted limit (or 5 mph if speed limit is less than 25 mph)
Slow to 10 mph below posted limit (or 15 mph if speed limit is less than 30 mph)
Maintain full posted cruising speed provided you activate four-way flashers
Slow down to exactly thirty-five miles per hour on all interstate highway lanes

bank_b_laws.rationale: TTC §545.157 requires drivers to vacate the lane closest to stopped emergency/work vehicles, or slow down to 20 mph below the posted limit (or 5 mph if limit < 25 mph).

bank_b_laws.domain: TRAFFIC LAWS & RULES OF THE ROAD
bank_b_laws.prompt: What blood alcohol concentration (BAC) defines legal intoxication per se for adult drivers in Texas?

options.text: An alcohol concentration of 0.08 or more in blood, breath, or urine sample
An alcohol concentration of 0.05 or more in blood, breath, or urine sample
An alcohol concentration of 0.10 or more in blood, breath, or urine sample
An alcohol concentration of 0.02 or more in blood, breath, or urine sample

bank_b_laws.rationale: Texas Penal Code §49.01(2)(B) establishes 0.08 BAC as the statutory per se limit for adult drivers, regardless of visible symptoms.

bank_b_laws.domain: TRAFFIC LAWS & RULES OF THE ROAD
bank_b_laws.prompt: Under the Texas Zero Tolerance law, what alcohol level constitutes DUI for a minor under age 21?

options.text: Any detectable amount of alcohol in the minor's system while driving a vehicle
Only when the minor's blood alcohol concentration exceeds the 0.08 adult limit
A BAC exceeding 0.05 measured during certified forensic laboratory blood tests
Zero Tolerance applies exclusively to minors operating commercial school buses

bank_b_laws.rationale: Under Texas Alcoholic Beverage Code §106.041, any detectable amount of alcohol in a minor driver's system constitutes DUI by a Minor.

bank_b_laws.domain: TRAFFIC LAWS & RULES OF THE ROAD
bank_b_laws.prompt: What is the administrative license suspension for refusing a chemical test after a first-offense DWI arrest?

options.text: 180 days administrative driver license suspension for a first chemical test refusal
30 days administrative driver license suspension for a first chemical test refusal
2 years administrative driver license suspension for a first chemical test refusal
Refusing a test carries zero administrative license suspension penalties in Texas

bank_b_laws.rationale: Under TTC §724.035, refusing to submit to a chemical breath or blood test results in an automatic 180-day license suspension on a first offense.

bank_b_laws.domain: TRAFFIC LAWS & RULES OF THE ROAD
bank_b_laws.prompt: Where may an unsealed container of alcohol be legally transported in a passenger car in Texas?

options.text: In the vehicle locked trunk, or behind the upright rear seats in an SUV without a trunk
Inside the center console compartment between the driver and front passenger
Inside the unlocked front dashboard glove box directly beneath the radio
Under the driver's seat provided the container is placed inside a brown paper sack

bank_b_laws.rationale: Under TPC §49.031, open containers are prohibited in the passenger area; they may only be transported in a locked glove box, locked trunk, or behind the last upright seat in vehicles lacking trunks.

bank_b_laws.domain: TRAFFIC LAWS & RULES OF THE ROAD
bank_b_laws.prompt: Under Texas law, which children must be secured in a child passenger safety seat system?

options.text: Children younger than 8 years old, unless taller than 4 feet 9 inches in height
Children younger than 5 years old, regardless of physical standing height
Children younger than 12 years old, unless weighing over eighty-five pounds
Children are required to use booster seats only until their fourth birthday

bank_b_laws.rationale: TTC §545.412 mandates child passenger safety seats for children younger than 8 years old unless they are taller than 4 feet 9 inches (57 inches).

bank_b_laws.domain: TRAFFIC LAWS & RULES OF THE ROAD
bank_b_laws.prompt: Under Texas Penal Code §22.10, when is leaving a child unattended inside a vehicle a criminal offense?

options.text: Child younger than 7 left unattended for >5 mins without someone ≥14 years old
Child younger than 12 left unattended for >15 mins while running errands
Only if the outdoor ambient temperature exceeds ninety degrees Fahrenheit
Leaving a child inside a parked car is never illegal if windows are cracked

bank_b_laws.rationale: TPC §22.10 makes it a misdemeanor to intentionally leave a child under 7 unattended for longer than 5 minutes without an individual at least 14 years old.

bank_b_laws.domain: TRAFFIC LAWS & RULES OF THE ROAD
bank_b_laws.prompt: At an uncontrolled 4-way intersection where two vehicles arrive simultaneously, who must yield?

options.text: The driver on the left must yield right-of-way to the vehicle on their right
The vehicle on the right must yield right-of-way to the vehicle on their left
The smaller passenger car always yields to larger commercial freight trucks
Both vehicles must remain stationary until a municipal police officer arrives

bank_b_laws.rationale: Under TTC §545.151, when two vehicles approach an intersection at approximately the same time, the driver on the left shall yield to the vehicle on the right.

bank_b_laws.domain: TRAFFIC LAWS & RULES OF THE ROAD
bank_b_laws.prompt: When is a driver on a divided highway with an unpaved median EXEMPT from stopping for a school bus?

options.text: When traveling in the opposite direction on a roadway divided by a physical barrier
Whenever traveling in the same direction on a four-lane highway with turn lanes
When driving during afternoon rush hour between five and six in the evening
Vehicles are never exempt from stopping for school buses under any circumstances

bank_b_laws.rationale: Under TTC §545.066(b), traffic traveling in the opposite direction on a separate roadway divided by a physical barrier or median is not required to stop.

bank_b_laws.domain: TRAFFIC LAWS & RULES OF THE ROAD
bank_b_laws.prompt: Under the Community Safety Education Act (Senate Bill 30), what should a driver do when pulled over at night?

options.text: Turn on interior dome light, roll down driver window, place hands on steering wheel
Exit the vehicle immediately and walk toward the patrol cruiser quickly
Reach under passenger seats to search for insurance cards before officer arrives
Rev the engine slightly to verify alternator voltage is charging battery

bank_b_laws.rationale: SB 30 instructs motorists to pull safely to the right, turn on the dome light at night, keep hands visibly on the steering wheel, and inform the officer before reaching for documents.

bank_b_laws.domain: TRAFFIC LAWS & RULES OF THE ROAD
bank_b_laws.prompt: What is the primary benefit of enrolling in the Texas Driving with Disabilities Program via Form VTR-214?

options.text: Alerts officers to communication impediments via TLETS before approaching vehicle
Exempts the driver from having to carry minimum state automotive liability insurance
Grants the vehicle permanent authorization to drive in carpool HOV lanes alone
Prohibits police officers from ever issuing traffic citations to the motorist

bank_b_laws.rationale: Form VTR-214 records a communication impediment in TLETS, alerting the officer prior to approaching the car to communicate with patience and avoid misunderstandings.

bank_b_laws.domain: TRAFFIC LAWS & RULES OF THE ROAD
bank_b_laws.prompt: What is the official toll-free telephone number for the National Human Trafficking Hotline under the Julia Wells Act?

options.text: 1-888-373-7888 (available 24/7, confidential, or text HELP to 233733 / BeFree)
1-800-555-0199 (available weekdays during municipal city business hours)
1-877-432-1100 (state vehicle title and registration customer hotline)
1-800-222-1222 (state toxic poison control center emergency helpline)

bank_b_laws.rationale: Under Texas Education Code §1001.1021, the National Human Trafficking Hotline is 1-888-373-7888 (or text HELP to 233733), offering 24/7 confidential reporting.

bank_b_laws.domain: TRAFFIC LAWS & RULES OF THE ROAD
bank_b_laws.prompt: Under Texas Transportation Code §545.104, at what minimum distance prior to turning or changing lanes must an operator signal?

options.text: Continuously for at least the last 100 feet before making the turn or maneuver
At least 500 feet on city streets and 1,000 feet on state highways
A minimum of three seconds regardless of speed, but no distance requirement applies
Signaling is optional in Texas if no vehicles are visible in the rear-view mirror

bank_b_laws.rationale: Under TTC §545.104(b), an operator intending to turn a vehicle right or left shall signal continuously for not less than the last 100 feet of movement.

bank_b_laws.domain: TRAFFIC LAWS & RULES OF THE ROAD
bank_b_laws.prompt: Under Texas Transportation Code §547.302, when are vehicle headlights legally required to be illuminated?

options.text: From 30 minutes after sunset to 30 minutes before sunrise, and whenever visibility is less than 1,000 feet
Only when driving on rural county roads that lack overhead municipal streetlights
Exclusively between midnight and 6:00 AM regardless of atmospheric weather conditions
Only when the temperature drops below freezing or snow accumulation begins

bank_b_laws.rationale: Under TTC §547.302, headlights must be lighted at night (30 min after sunset to 30 min before sunrise) and when visibility is below 1,000 feet.

bank_b_laws.domain: TRAFFIC LAWS & RULES OF THE ROAD
bank_b_laws.prompt: Under Texas law (TTC §547.333), at what distance must an operator dim high-beam headlights when approaching an oncoming vehicle?

options.text: Within 500 feet of an approaching oncoming vehicle, and within 300 feet when following behind another vehicle
Within 1,000 feet of an oncoming vehicle and 500 feet when following
Only when the oncoming driver flashes their high beams first
Dimming high beams is required exclusively on divided multilane interstate highways

bank_b_laws.rationale: TTC §547.333 mandates dimming high beams within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle and within 300 feet when following.

bank_b_laws.domain: TRAFFIC LAWS & RULES OF THE ROAD
bank_b_laws.prompt: Under the Texas Move Over / Slow Down Law (TTC §545.157), what must a driver do when passing a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights?

options.text: Vacate the lane closest to the emergency vehicle if possible, or reduce speed to 20 mph below posted limit
Accelerate briskly past the scene to prevent rubbernecking traffic congestion
Come to a complete stop in your lane until emergency personnel wave you forward
Sound your vehicle horn to alert emergency workers to your approach

bank_b_laws.rationale: TTC §545.157 requires drivers to move out of the adjacent lane or slow down to 20 mph below the posted speed limit (or 5 mph if limit is under 25 mph).

bank_b_laws.domain: TRAFFIC LAWS & RULES OF THE ROAD
bank_b_laws.prompt: Under Texas Transportation Code §545.425, what is the law regarding cell phone use while operating a vehicle in an active school zone?

options.text: Using a wireless communication device in a school zone is strictly prohibited unless hands-free or stopped
Drivers may send text messages if their vehicle is traveling below 15 miles per hour
Cell phone use is prohibited only during morning arrival hours, but permitted during afternoon dismissal
Cell phones may be used freely as long as the driver maintains one hand on the steering wheel

bank_b_laws.rationale: TTC §545.425 strictly prohibits handheld wireless communication devices in active school-crossing zones unless using a hands-free device or vehicle is stopped.

bank_b_laws.domain: TRAFFIC LAWS & RULES OF THE ROAD
bank_b_laws.prompt: What is the minimum safe following distance recommended by Texas defensive driving standards under ideal daytime conditions?

options.text: A minimum of 3 to 4 seconds behind the vehicle immediately ahead
Exactly one car length for every 30 miles per hour of vehicle speed
One half second, provided your vehicle is equipped with anti-lock brakes
Ten feet for every ten miles per hour on city streets

bank_b_laws.rationale: Under TDLR curriculum standards, a 3 to 4 second following distance is the baseline standard for dry pavement under ideal conditions.

bank_b_laws.domain: TRAFFIC LAWS & RULES OF THE ROAD
bank_b_laws.prompt: Under Texas Transportation Code §545.352, what is the default statutory speed limit in an urban district unless posted otherwise?

options.text: 30 miles per hour on streets, and 15 miles per hour in urban alleys
45 miles per hour on all paved residential neighborhood roadways
20 miles per hour on all city streets without dividing curbs
55 miles per hour on both city streets and frontage roads

bank_b_laws.rationale: Under TTC §545.352(b)(1), the prima facie speed limit in an urban district is 30 mph, and 15 mph in an alley.

bank_b_laws.domain: TRAFFIC LAWS & RULES OF THE ROAD
bank_b_laws.prompt: What does the Texas 'Basic Speed Rule' (TTC §545.351) legally require of all drivers?

options.text: No person may drive at a speed greater than is reasonable and prudent under existing roadway and weather conditions
Drivers must always travel at exactly the maximum posted numerical speed limit
Drivers may exceed posted speed limits when passing slower commercial vehicles on rural highways
Vehicle speed is legally unrestricted on farm-to-market roads between midnight and 5:00 AM

bank_b_laws.rationale: Under TTC §545.351, driving at an unreasonable or imprudent speed is illegal even if the speed is below the posted numerical limit.

bank_b_laws.domain: TRAFFIC LAWS & RULES OF THE ROAD
bank_b_laws.prompt: At an intersection not controlled by traffic signals or signs, an unpaved road intersects with a paved road. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: Traffic on the paved road has the right-of-way; vehicles on the unpaved road must yield
Traffic on the unpaved road has right-of-way because loose gravel requires longer stopping distance
Whichever vehicle arrives at the intersection boundary line first has unconditional right-of-way
Drivers on both roads must stop and alternate entry in single-file formation

bank_b_laws.rationale: Under TTC §545.151(a)(2), an operator on an unpaved road approaching an intersection with a paved road must yield to traffic on the paved road.

bank_b_laws.domain: TRAFFIC LAWS & RULES OF THE ROAD
bank_b_laws.prompt: Under Texas Transportation Code §545.302, within what minimum distance of a fire hydrant is stopping, standing, or parking prohibited?

options.text: Within 15 feet of a fire hydrant
Within 30 feet of a fire hydrant
Within 5 feet of a fire hydrant
Within 50 feet of a fire hydrant

bank_b_laws.rationale: Under TTC §545.302(b)(1), an operator may not stand or park an occupied or unoccupied vehicle within 15 feet of a fire hydrant.

bank_b_laws.domain: TRAFFIC LAWS & RULES OF THE ROAD
bank_b_laws.prompt: Under Texas Transportation Code §545.302, within what distance of a stop sign, yield sign, or flashing traffic signal is parking prohibited?

options.text: Within 30 feet upon the approach to any flashing beacon, stop sign, or traffic control signal
Within 10 feet of a stop sign or traffic signal
Within 75 feet on both sides of the street
Parking near stop signs is permitted if vehicle hazard warning lights are flashing

bank_b_laws.rationale: Under TTC §545.302(b)(4), parking within 30 feet of any flashing beacon, stop sign, or traffic-control signal is strictly prohibited.

bank_b_laws.domain: TRAFFIC LAWS & RULES OF THE ROAD
bank_b_laws.prompt: Under Texas law (TTC §545.066), what must a driver do when approaching a school bus displaying visual flashing red lights and an extended stop arm?

options.text: Stop before reaching the bus and remain stopped until lights cease flashing or the driver signals to proceed
Slow to 15 miles per hour and pass with extreme caution if no children are in the road
Stop only if traveling in the same direction directly behind the school bus
Tap the horn to alert the bus driver before proceeding through the blind spot

bank_b_laws.rationale: Under TTC §545.066, an operator approaching a stopped school bus operating flashing visual signals must stop and not proceed until the bus resumes motion.

bank_b_laws.domain: TRAFFIC LAWS & RULES OF THE ROAD
bank_b_laws.prompt: Under Texas law (TTC §552.003), who has the right-of-way when a pedestrian is in a crosswalk on the half of the roadway where the vehicle is traveling?

options.text: The driver must yield right-of-way and stop to let the pedestrian cross safely
Vehicles have the right-of-way unless the pedestrian is carrying a white cane or guide dog
The pedestrian must yield to approaching vehicles traveling at the posted speed limit
Both driver and pedestrian have equal right-of-way determined by who moves first

bank_b_laws.rationale: TTC §552.003 requires motorists to yield the right-of-way to a pedestrian crossing in a crosswalk if traffic signals are not in place.

bank_b_laws.domain: TRAFFIC LAWS & RULES OF THE ROAD
bank_b_laws.prompt: Under Texas Transportation Code §545.251, at what distance from the nearest rail of a railroad crossing must a driver stop when signals are active?

options.text: Between 15 feet and 50 feet from the nearest rail
Between 5 feet and 10 feet from the nearest rail
Exactly 100 feet from the crossing gate barrier
At least 150 feet if driving a vehicle pulling a trailer

bank_b_laws.rationale: TTC §545.251 mandates that an operator approaching a railroad crossing stop not closer than 15 feet or farther than 50 feet from the nearest rail.

bank_b_laws.domain: TRAFFIC LAWS & RULES OF THE ROAD
bank_b_laws.prompt: Under Texas Transportation Code §550.026, when must an operator immediately report a motor vehicle collision to local law enforcement?

options.text: If the collision results in injury, death, or damage to a vehicle to the extent it cannot be normally and safely driven
Only if total property damage is estimated by insurance adjusters to exceed $10,000
Exclusively when commercial vehicles or hazardous chemical materials are involved
Crash reporting is voluntary in Texas if both drivers exchange personal phone numbers

bank_b_laws.rationale: Under TTC §550.026, the operator of a vehicle involved in an accident resulting in injury, death, or inoperable vehicle damage must immediately report it.

bank_b_laws.domain: TRAFFIC LAWS & RULES OF THE ROAD
bank_b_laws.prompt: Under Texas Transportation Code §545.413, who in a passenger vehicle is legally required to wear a safety belt?

options.text: The driver and all passengers in all seating positions equipped with a safety belt
Only the driver and front-seat passenger; rear passengers are exempt if over 18
Only passengers riding on multi-lane interstate highways with speeds over 65 mph
Safety belt use is required only during nighttime hours between sunset and sunrise

bank_b_laws.rationale: Texas has a primary seat belt law (TTC §545.413): all occupants in all passenger vehicle seating positions must wear seat belts.

bank_b_laws.domain: TRAFFIC LAWS & RULES OF THE ROAD
bank_b_laws.prompt: Under Texas law (TTC §545.301), if a vehicle must be stopped on a highway outside a business or residence district, what width of roadway must remain clear?

options.text: An unobstructed roadway width of at least 20 feet opposite the vehicle for free passage of other vehicles
A clear space of at least 50 feet in front of and behind the vehicle
At least 10 feet from the yellow centerline regardless of shoulder width
No clearance is required if the driver raises the vehicle hood

bank_b_laws.rationale: Under TTC §545.301(a)(1), parking outside an urban district requires leaving an unobstructed width of at least 20 feet for traffic passage.

bank_b_laws.domain: TRAFFIC LAWS & RULES OF THE ROAD
bank_b_laws.prompt: Under Texas Penal Code §49.031, what constitutes a violation of the Open Container law?

options.text: Knowingly possessing an open container of alcohol in the passenger area of a motor vehicle located on a public highway, whether parked or moving
Transporting unopened sealed cans of beer inside a cardboard box in the passenger seat
Carrying an open beverage container in the locked trunk of a passenger sedan
Passengers drinking beverages in the passenger compartment of a licensed commercial limousine

bank_b_laws.rationale: Texas Penal Code §49.031 makes it a Class C misdemeanor to possess an open alcoholic container in the passenger area of a vehicle on a public roadway.

bank_b_laws.domain: TRAFFIC LAWS & RULES OF THE ROAD
bank_b_laws.prompt: Under Texas vehicle safety inspection standards (TTC §547.612), what is the minimum legal tire tread depth required on passenger tires?

options.text: 2/32 of an inch (1.6 mm) of remaining tread depth measured in any two adjacent major tread grooves
4/32 of an inch across the entire shoulder area only
1/16 of an inch during summer months and 1/8 of an inch during winter
Tread depth is unregulated in Texas as long as the tire holds air pressure

bank_b_laws.rationale: Under Texas vehicle inspection criteria and TTC §547.612, tires must have at least 2/32 inch tread depth to pass state inspection.

bank_b_laws.domain: TRAFFIC LAWS & RULES OF THE ROAD
bank_b_laws.prompt: If your vehicle begins to hydroplane (water-skiing across wet pavement with loss of traction), what is the correct driver reaction?

options.text: Ease foot off the accelerator smoothly, steer in the direction of the skid, and avoid slamming on brakes
Slam hard on the service brake pedal immediately and jerk the wheel sharply away from the road shoulder
Accelerate firmly to regain tire grip through hydrodynamic wheel rotation
Engage the emergency parking brake lever while downshifting to first gear

bank_b_laws.rationale: TDLR defensive driving guidelines mandate smoothly releasing the accelerator without panic braking to allow tires to regain direct pavement contact.
